## Reading the misses

Phase 7's drift test raised false alarms on 11.6% of clean test runs against a 5% target (not met). Phase 7b's new rule failed its pre-registered criterion C1 on FD004: 19.5% and 13.9% of clean runs flagged (synchronized and staggered fleets) against a 5% limit. Both are reported, not re-tuned.

## Technical highlights by phase

- **Baselines (Phase 4, FD001):** XGBoost reaches 15.08 RMSE (bootstrap interval 12.2-17.9), against a fleet average (41.9) and an age-only rule (31.2). Near-failure errors are in [MODEL_METRICS.md](MODEL_METRICS.md).

- **Deep models (Phase 5, FD001):** the LSTM reaches 13.30 RMSE (bootstrap interval 10.5-16.1), better than XGBoost on paper but not significantly, so XGBoost stayed published. Raw MC-dropout intervals covered only 76% of validation truths at a nominal 90%; one scale factor learned on validation brought test coverage to 82%.

- **Confirmation (Phase 5b, FD003):** the LSTM reaches 12.66 RMSE against XGBoost's 15.50. Pooled over FD001 and FD003 its advantage is 2.31 cycles RMSE (bootstrap interval 0.76-4.05, Holm p 0.007) and 2.76 vs 4.60 cycles near failure, so the LSTM is now the published model. The two-factor interval rule covers 86% of FD003 test engines.

- **Maintenance (Phase 6, simulated plant):** the predictive policy reaches 98.2% simulated OEE with 8 unplanned failures, against 95.2% for run to failure (200 failures) and 97.8% for a fixed service interval (21 failures, and 2.7 times as much useful life thrown away).

- **Monitoring (Phase 7):** drift is a KS test per sensor on per-engine means, Holm-corrected, alpha 0.01; retraining triggers when rolling RMSE exceeds 1.45 x validation RMSE. The drift test fired on 11.6% of clean test runs against a 5% target.

- **Monitoring re-tested (Phase 7b):** clean-run flags 0.0% / 0.9% on FD002 and 19.5% / 13.9% on FD004 (synchronized / staggered fleets), against a 5% limit: passed on FD002, failed on FD004.
